{{Short description|German mathematician}}
{{Use dmy dates|date=October 2019}}
{{Use British English|date=October 2019}}
'''Rudolf Schauffler''' (born 11 August 1889 in [[Ulm]]– died 6 February 1968) was a German mathematician, who was most notable for being the nominal head of the [[Linguistics]] and [[Cryptanalysis]] section of [[Pers Z S]], the [[Signals intelligence|Signal Intelligence Agency]] of the [[Foreign Office (Germany)|German Foreign Office]] ({{langx|de|Auswärtiges Amt}}) before and during [[World War II]].<ref name="WeirudZabell">{{cite journal |last1=Weierud |first1=Frode |last2=Zabell |first2=Sandy |title=German mathematicians and cryptology in WWII |journal=Cryptologia |date=6 June 2019 |volume=44 |issue=2 |pages=97–171 |doi=10.1080/01611194.2019.1600076|s2cid=198336556 }}</ref>

==Life==
Before [[World War I]], Schauffler had been a schoolmaster after studying mathematics, physics and languages at the [[University of Tübingen]] and the [[Ludwig-Maximilians-Universität München]].<ref name="WeirudZabell"/> During World War I, he was [[Chemical warfare|gassed]].<ref name="i-22">{{cite book |url=https://archive.org/stream/ticom/TicomI-22#page/n0/mode/2up |title=TICOM I-22 Interrogation of German Cryptographers of Pers ZS Department of the Auswäertiges Amt. |date=2 July 1945 |publisher=TICOM |format=PDF |access-date=11 October 2019}}{{PD-notice}}</ref> During the first world war, Schauffler worked as a cryptanalyst at the German army headquarters.<ref name="khan_1st">{{cite book |last1=David |first1=Kahn |title=The Codebreakers: The Story of Secret Writing |date=1967 |publisher=Macmillan Company |location=New york |isbn=9780297767855 |page=437 |edition=1st}}</ref> After the war, Schauffler found the work of schoolmaster to be too difficult and decided to join Pers Z S. Schauffler was recruited by [[Kurt Selchow]] and joined on 1 December 1918.<ref name="i-22"/> Selchow also recruited Werner Kunze, Adolf Paschke, Karl Zastrow, Wilhelm Brandes, and Ernst Hoffmann for the unit as he had known them during the war.<ref name="twooheight">{{cite web |url=https://archive.org/details/ticom/TicomI-208|title=TICOM I-208 Interrogation report on Kurt Selchow, Former head of the Pers ZS Department of the German Ministry of Foreign Affairs 27 October 1947 |publisher=TICOM |website=Internet Archive|format=PDF |access-date=25 January 2025|page=2}}{{PD-notice}}</ref>

Although he did not have a [[Doctor of Philosophy]] degree nor did he [[Habilitation|habilitate]] while in office, Schauffler was most definitely a real mathematician.<ref name="WeirudZabell"/> The [[mathematician]] and cryptographer [[Erich Hüttenhain]] in his evaluation of Schauffler regarded him as a ''true scientist''.<ref>{{cite web |title=TICOM I-31:Detailed interrogations of Dr. Hüttenhain, formerly head of research section of OKW/Chi, at Flensburg on 18-21 June 1945 |page=11 |url=https://archive.org/details/ticom/TicomI-31/ |website=Internet Archive |accessdate=11 June 2018}}{{PD-notice}}</ref>

[[File:Die Handelsmaschine, 1923.jpg|thumb|right|"Die Handelsmaschine", one of the early cipher machines examined by Schauffler]]
Very early in his career, he wrote two papers in 1917 and 1921 for the [[Mathematische Annalen]] mathematical research journal. After the war he wrote a thesis in 1941 but did not submit it until 1947 to [[Marburg University]]. The subject was on cryptography: ''An application of cyclic permutations and their theory''  (German: Eine Anwendung zyklischer Permutationen und ihre Theorie). It had not been submitted due to the contents being secret.<ref name="WeirudZabell"/> He was promoted to [[Doctor of Philosophy]] in 1948. In 1956 and 1957, he wrote two further papers, the first of these was on the theory of [[Check digit]] systems.<ref name="WeirudZabell"/>

In 1967, the historian [[David Kahn (writer)|David Kahn]] interviewed Schauffler in his apartment for his 1967 book, ''[[The Codebreakers]]'' and found it most depressing.<ref name="WeirudZabell"/> Kahn wrote of Schauffler:<ref>{{cite book |last1=David |first1=Kahn |title=The Codebreakers: The Story of Secret Writing |date=1967 |publisher=Macmillan Company |location=New york |isbn=9780297767855 |page=11 |edition=1st}}</ref>

:''Elderly, not old, but broken by sickness and the ersatz food of the war years, he shuffled around his chilly apartment, barely able to put a pot of water on for tea. As rain dripped slowly from the gray sky, he ended our talk by saying, “A bridge builder can see what he has done for his countrymen, but we (German codebreakers) cannot tell whether our life was worth anything.”''<ref>Kahn, D. 1967. How one Bucknellian wrote his book. The Bucknell Alumnus, November, p.10–14.</ref>

==Career==
 
Initially, Schauffler worked on cryptographic metholologies. During the period from 1921 to 1923, Schauffler worked as part a team that included [[Werner Kunze]] on the development of a [[one-time pad]] system for the use by the Foreign Office.<ref>{{cite book |last1=David |first1=Kahn |title=The Codebreakers: The Story of Secret Writing |date=1967 |publisher=Macmillan Company |location=New york |isbn=9780297767855 |pages=402–403 |edition=1st}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |last1=van der Meulen |first1=Michael |title=Cryptology in the Early Bundesrepublik |journal=Cryptologia |date=4 June 2010 |volume=20 |issue=3 |pages=202–222 |doi=10.1080/0161-119691884915}}</ref> He later became interested in [[Chinese language|Chinese]] and [[Japanese language|Japanese]] languages while sharing an office with [[Emil Krebs]],<ref>{{cite book |last1=Hoffmann |first1=Eckhard |last2=Harrassowitz (Wiesbaden) |first2=Otto |title=Emil Krebs : ein Sprachgenie im Dienste der Diplomatie |date=2017 |publisher=Harrassowitz Verlag |location=Wiesbaden |isbn=9783447107402 |language=German|oclc=1100371401}}</ref> who taught him, eventually becoming a specialist in both languages over a period of twenty years.<ref name="WeirudZabell"/> Schauffler later focused on [[Basic research|theoretical research]] that became his main field of interest.<ref>I-22 Paragraph 8</ref> In 1923, he examined the [[Rotor machine|rotor cipher machine]], the [[Enigma machine]], specifically the early design known as "Die Handelsmaschine" (The trading machine) and wrote a report explaining the dangers of [[decipherment]].<ref>I-22 Paragraph 8</ref> 

He later edited the in-house journal, ''Scientific Writings of the [[Dahlem (Berlin)|Dahlem]] Special Service'', (German:Wissenschaftliche Schriften des Sonderdienstes Dahlem).<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.nsa.gov/Portals/70/documents/news-features/declassified-documents/european-axis-sigint/Volume_3_supreme_command_sigint_agency.pdf |title=European Axis Signals Intelligence World War 2 Volume 3 |publisher=TICOM |accessdate=31 January 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130918212307/http://www.nsa.gov/public_info/_files/european_axis_sigint/Volume_3_supreme_command_sigint_agency.pdf |archive-date=18 September 2013|page=100 }}{{PD-notice}}</ref>

In 1950, the [[Federal Foreign Office]] tasked Selchow along with Schauffler, [[Erich Hüttenhain]] and [[Heinz Kuntze]] to form a cryptographic service under the direction of Adolf Paschke that was called Section 114.<ref name="AidWiebes2001">{{cite book|author1=Matthew M. Aid|author2=Cees Wiebes|title=Secrets of Signals Intelligence During the Cold War and Beyond|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=KaR5O4PKNAoC&pg=PA160|accessdate=9 February 2019|year=2001 |publisher=Psychology Press |isbn=978-0-7146-5176-7|page=160}}</ref> The service was to act as a cypher bureau for the Central office of Encryption (ZfCh) ({{langx|de|Zentralstelle für das Chiffrierwesen}}) that had been previously created in 1947 and was located at [[Camp King]]. In 1955, the unit was disbanded as [[West Germany]] was rearming, and a new unit was to be created.<ref name="AidWiebes2001"/> In 1956 all the equipment and resources of the unit were transferred to the [[Federal Intelligence Service (Germany)]].<ref name="AidWiebes2001"/> In 1989 the unit was renamed to ZFI ({{langx|de|Zentralstelle für Sicherheit in der Informationstechnik}}). In 1991, it became the BSI ([[Federal Office for Information Security]])
